summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), inactive IBD, celiac disease, and hypertension was admitted for acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain and fever. Initial evaluation revealed elevated liver enzymes and gallstones without cholecystitis on ultrasound. An MRCP showed progression of PSC with active bile duct inflammation but no malignancy or obstruction. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics, later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin, and her symptoms improved significantly. She remained stable throughout the hospitalization, with no complications, and was discharged home with a 12-day course of antibiotics and instructions to follow up with her gastroenterologist in two weeks.
